Parametric Bootstrap Predictive Distribution

Source: R/predict_objects.R
pred_bootstrap.Rd

The parametric bootstrap predictive distribution of Harris (1989): n responses are simulated from the fit with the random effects drawn afresh, each response is refitted, and the family at each refit is averaged over the effects. It does not rely on the normal approximation of pred_averaged(), and it costs n refits.

Usage

pred_bootstrap(n = 200L, refit = c("coefficients", "full"))

Arguments

n

The number of replicas, a single positive whole number. The default is 200.

refit

"coefficients" (the default), refitting each replica at the fit's hyperparameters, or "full", choosing them again.

Value

An S7 object of class PredBootstrap, inheriting from predictive_type(), with the properties label, n (an integer) and refit.

Details

With refit = "coefficients" each replica is refitted at the fit's hyperparameters. With refit = "full" the hyperparameters are chosen again on every replica, so their uncertainty enters the interval as well, at the cost of a whole fit per replica. The bootstrap is rejected for a model with a block that moves with its coefficients, for a response that is not one number per observation, and, with refit = "full", for a cross-validated criterion. The replicas use the random number generator of the session, so set.seed() before the call reproduces them. If the fit holds a stored parametric bootstrap (add_bootstrap()) with the same refit, its first n replicates are used and nothing is refitted; an entry with fewer than n replicates is extended and stored again. With modelterms7::random() terms the entry is used when random sets every one of them aside and the entry holds the refitted random effects. See predictive_distributions and predictive_bootstrap().

References

Harris, I. R. (1989). Predictive fit for natural exponential families. Biometrika, 76, 675–684.

See also

pred_averaged(), pred_plugin(), prediction_interval(), predictive_distributions.

Examples

set.seed(2)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(30))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(30, sd = 0.5)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
predict(fit, what = "response", newdata = data.frame(x = 0.5),
        interval = prediction_interval(
          predictive = pred_bootstrap(n = 20, refit = "coefficients")))
#>        fit        se     lower    upper
#> 1 1.547902 0.5891418 0.3767825 2.695134
